settings.name_in_paper: Contextual causal bandits with non-manipulable variables (Bayesian formulation)
unmapped: Known causal graph (DAG) without latent confounders; actions are POMIS-induced interventions do(X=x) with some variables non-manipulable
Unknown parameter is the set of CPTs of the observational distribution with independent Dirichlet priors
Learner observes all non-intervened variables after each intervention (richer than reward-only feedback)
Contexts are ancestrally closed variables of the SCM observed before action; may be informative about theta
Regret against context-dependent oracle mapping Pi*(c)
settings.definition_quote: We study contextual causal bandits with non-manipulable variables under the assumption that the causal graph is known and contains no latent confounders. At each round, context variables are observed before the learner selects an intervention. The learner subsequently observes the reward and the remaining observed variables in the causal graph.

symbols.Gamma: uniform upper bound on the square root of the information ratio Gamma_t

conditions: no latent confounders, known causal graph

source.label: thm1
source.quote: The mean cumulative Bayesian regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg: thom} is bounded for any $T \in \mathbb{N}$ as follows, where $\Gamma \geq \Gamma_t$ for all $t \in \{1,\ldots,T\}$: ... \leq \Gamma \sqrt{H(\Pi^\star) \, T}.

results.notes: Comparator is the oracle context-to-action mapping Pi*; mapped to best_policy. Instance-free bound in terms of prior entropy.

source.label: crr_reg
source.quote: Suppose that the context space $\mathcal{C}$ is finite. The mean cumulative Bayesian regret for Algorithm~\ref{alg: thom} is bounded for any $T \in \mathbb{N}$ as follows: ... \leq \sqrt{\frac{T|\mathcal{A}| |\mathcal{C}|\log\!|\mathcal{A}|}{2}}.

results.notes: Uses Gamma_t^2 <= |A|/2 and H(Pi*) <= |C| log|A|. Intermediate bound sqrt(|A|/2 H(Pi*) T) also derived.

symbols.H_Pi: entropy of the optimal context-to-action mapping Pi* under the prior
symbols.Gamma_sum: sum_t E[gamma_t 1_{E_t}], gamma_t the sup deviation of the information ratio over the Monte Carlo confidence sets

conditions: no latent confounders, known causal graph
tuning: N posterior Monte Carlo samples per round
results.notes: delta here is the algorithm's overall confidence delta'. Bound may be vacuous if gamma_t = infinity. Regret is in expectation (not high-probability).

symbols.H_Pi: entropy of the optimal context-to-action mapping Pi* under the prior

conditions: Delta_t(a|c_t) and g_t(a|c_t) computed exactly each round

source.label: cor:oracle
source.quote: Suppose that $\Delta_t(a\mid\mathbf{c}_t)$ and $g_t(a\mid\mathbf{c}_t)$ can be computed exactly at every round and IDS minimizes the exact information ratio. Then, for any $T\in\mathbb{N}$, the mean cumulative regret satisfies ... \leq \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{A}|}{2}\,T\,H(\Pi^\star)}.

results.notes: Oracle IDS; with finite contexts H(Pi*) <= |C| log |A|.
